Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testSSENonNegative` fails because the method `SimpleRegression.getSumSquaredErrors()` returns a negative value. The code for `getSumSquaredErrors()` is:
```java
return sumYY - sumXY * sumXY / sumXX;
```
This value theoretically corresponds to the residual sum of squares (SSE) in regression analysis and should be non-negative.

Looking at the `addData(double x, double y)` method, the sums `sumXX`, `sumYY`, and `sumXY` are updated incrementally on each new data point, with formulas that aim to maintain running sums based on deviations from current means (`xbar` and `ybar`). The formulas used normalize by `n / (n+1)`.

The test data points show x-values in large magnitude (around 110) and y-values around 8900. The issue in the bug report suggests that using x-values without scaling (or using different magnitudes for x as the user tried with x and x2 arrays) leads to negative SSE values, which is unexpected.

A key insight is that `sumXX` may be very small due to floating point precision or calculation error with the current incremental formula. If `sumXX` is very close to zero or the intermediate calculation `sumXY * sumXY / sumXX` is slightly more than `sumYY` due to floating point inaccuracies, the returned SSE would be negative.

Hence, the bug occurs due to precision errors or numerical instability in the incremental update formulas in `addData`, which result in an invalid (negative) residual sum of squares returned by `getSumSquaredErrors()`.

Next, examining more of the formula or the context of the variables might be needed to confirm and locate more susceptible parts of the calculation. But from the evidence, the root cause is the floating-point arithmetic and incremental sum update scheme leading to inconsistent state.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
